grading_system.evidence: To meet graduation requirements, students demonstrate proficiency through a minimum of the above courses and/or by accessing equivalent learning through Flexible Pathways. ... students must attain an overall course score of 2.01 or higher.
grading_system.proficiency_scale: 0-4 summative scale (4 Exemplary, 3 Proficient, 2 Approaching, 1 Beginning, 0 No Evidence); course scores also on this scale

schedule.evidence: The Drop/Add period is normally one week BEFORE and AFTER the new semester begins. Full-year courses are also listed. The catalog does not state blocks, periods, or how many courses run at once.

credit_definition.text: 1.0 credit = a full-year course with 9+ performance indicators; 0.5 credit = a semester course with 4-8 performance indicators.
credit_definition.evidence: For a ½ credit course, 4-8 PIs (content and Habits of Success) are offered and assessed. For a 1 credit course 9+ PIs (content and Habits of Success) are offered and assessed.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog credits are standard credits (1.0 = full-year course, 0.5 = semester course); no conversion needed. Distribution: English 4, science 3, math 3, global studies 3 (1 US History), fine arts 1, health 0.5, PE 1.5, electives 5.5. Proficiency in each Graduation Proficiency is also required.

flexible_pathways_listed: dual enrollment (up to seven VSU/CCV classes, 21 credits, free, taught at NMHS)
early college (Norwich University or CCV, senior year)
notes: Source is the PDF program of studies (phase2/text, PDF page markers used as page numbers; printed page numbers are one lower). Graduation is proficiency-based (PBGRs) with the course-credit distribution listed as 'TOTAL: 21.5' on PDF p.14. Hybrid is a judgment: credit distribution and proficiency in each graduation proficiency are both required (p.14); the catalog does not state a total credit count separate from the distribution. Habits of Success (cross-curricular) are required for graduation. A conversion chart to traditional GPA exists for college applications (p.11); it is not used for credit. Students who attain below 2.01 (B-) do not receive credit in CVSU (p.11). Schedule structure is not stated in the catalog. Early graduation requires written request (p.15). Senior Seminar is a required senior course (p.21 area).
